description: Machine-readable configuration for the self-tcb-reduction-driver: an SL that DRIVES (monitors) the self-tcb-reduction base loop. When the base loop hits a WALL (a \trusted stub it cannot convert and that measurement shows is not a cheap win), this meta-loop runs the review-and-break workflow — write a self-contained SOTA report XXX.md, get an INDEPENDENT XXX-response.md from a fable reviewer blind to the sub-loop, synthesize XXX-impl.md, then execute it spike-gated with every agent claim re-verified against the base loop's three L-planes. Companion: config/skills/self-tcb-reduction-driver/SKILL.md, self-tcb-reduction (the base loop), sl-monitoring-sl, sl-builder.
deliverable: Per wall XXX: RESOLVED with one of exactly two gate-defined verdicts — BROKEN (>=1 \trusted stub behind the wall converts to a verified body, full base-loop gate battery green, count strictly down, ledger unchanged) or CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY (a genuine limit, proven by the impl plan's make-or-break spike REFUTING the build before any emitter edit, recorded with a reproducible reason + a one-line lesson). Never a third verdict; never 'grind until done'.
correct_means: the report XXX.md states nothing L refutes (every claim reproducible from cited evidence)
XXX-response.md was authored WITHOUT the sub-loop's rationale in context (fable barrier) AND cites >=1 independent oracle artifact
XXX-impl.md's FIRST action is a make-or-break spike (measure-before-build) with an explicit refutation exit
every executing agent's claim is re-verified FRESH by the driver-verifier against the three L-planes
the final verdict is BROKEN (gates green) or CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY (spike refuted) — gate-defined, never self-declared

coherent_and_wrong_guards.risk: the reviewer rubber-stamps a wrong wall report
coherent_and_wrong_guards.caught_by: Gate R (reviewer gets L not just prose; independence via the fable barrier; >=1 oracle artifact required)

coherent_and_wrong_guards.risk: a build-first plan is executed to sprawl on an impossible wall
coherent_and_wrong_guards.caught_by: Gate P (spike-first + refutation exit) + Gate S (the spike runs)

coherent_and_wrong_guards.risk: an executor's self-reported gate result is accepted (--fun-only, ugrep count, 'byte-inert' premise)
coherent_and_wrong_guards.caught_by: the three-L-plane driver-verifier (Gate B/C); count via grep -F

coherent_and_wrong_guards.risk: an over-broad lesson ('all .values() are walls') enters the store
coherent_and_wrong_guards.caught_by: Gate S-lesson (trigger/validity test -> carve-out, never keep-whole)

coherent_and_wrong_guards.risk: the expensive cycle fires on a cheap win or a known boundary (cost blowout)
coherent_and_wrong_guards.caught_by: Gate W (escalate only a measured, non-cheap, not-already-CERTIFIED wall, and only after the cheap queue is drained)

priority.rule: DRAIN CHEAP WINS FIRST; break walls only when nothing cheap remains. Non-negotiable per iteration.
priority.rationale: wall-breaking (report -> fable review -> impl -> execute) is EXPENSIVE and yields at most one stub; a cheap conversion is one gate battery and yields one stub too — so every remaining cheap win is converted BEFORE any wall is escalated.
priority.phase_1_drain: repeatedly ask the base loop for the next cheap stub (cheap_win == true under measure-before-build) and convert it (full gate battery, driver-verified, committed). Stay in Phase 1 while the base loop returns a cheap stub.
priority.phase_2_break: ONLY when the base loop reports no_cheap_remaining does the driver escalate ONE wall (Gate W) through the full cycle. After a wall resolves (BROKEN or CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY) RETURN to Phase 1 and re-drain before the next wall (a BROKEN wall often unlocks cheap follow-ons).
priority.loop_shape: drain all cheap -> break one wall -> drain all cheap again -> break the next wall -> ...; terminates at floor (no cheap stub AND every wall BROKEN or CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY).

interactive.behavior: run ONE driver iteration (loop_steps), present the outcome, STOP (the user drives the cadence). Gate W may present its escalate/decline decision.

autonomous_time_boxed.trigger: invocation WITH a duration ('... for 2 hours' / '... for 90 min' / '... for 45m')
autonomous_time_boxed.behavior: iterate walls back-to-back with NO per-iteration prompting until a wall-clock deadline, committing each increment.

setup.why_persist: the deadline file survives context summarization across a long run — it is the single source of truth the next context window re-reads; do NOT hold it only in context
setup.announce: Autonomous driver: running until <deadline>. Iterating walls; committing each increment; no prompts until the deadline or you interrupt.

iteration: clock check: NOW=date +%s; DL=cat .driver-deadline; if NOW>=DL -> finish. Reserve headroom: do not START a full cycle that cannot finish before the deadline.

Phase 1: run the base loop as a SUB-AGENT non-interactively to convert the next cheap stub (no §11 menu); on convert -> driver-verifier re-checks the three L-planes, COMMIT, stay in Phase 1; repeat until no_cheap_remaining.
Phase 2 (only on no_cheap_remaining): Gate W -> pick ONE residual wall, run the full cycle (steps 3-8), commit the outcome, RETURN to Phase 1.
commit EVERY increment immediately (never a dirty tree between iterations; revert a sprawling/refuted build to clean before committing its finding).
Gate S-lesson on any consolidated lesson -> wall-lessons.md; next iteration.

finish.summary: emit ONE summary: walls RESOLVED (BROKEN vs CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY), conversions + count delta, lessons banked, unpushed-commit count. Do NOT auto-push (push only on an explicit push/push-it); list what is ready to push.
finish.early_stop: if the frontier reaches floor BEFORE the deadline, STOP EARLY and say so — do not spin on non-walls to burn the clock.

discipline: the gate battery is UNCHANGED — autonomous runs faster by not prompting, never by skipping a gate; a speed-motivated --fun-only accept is forbidden.

cross-turn continuation: when context fills before the deadline the harness summarizes and continues; the persisted .driver-deadline is how the next window knows to keep going and when to stop (re-read each iteration, do not re-ask).
interruptibility: a user message mid-run is honored immediately; each committed increment is a clean interrupt boundary.

escalate-not-thrash, time-aware: a per-wall attempt budget applies; do not START a full cycle whose fable-review + spike cannot finish before the deadline — defer it and spend the tail on cheaper items.

sources: the base loop's contract discipline (self-tcb-reduction.md, triage-ranked-tcb.md, §10 lessons: type-safety+frame contract shape; measure-before-build; no-unused-facade; coupling rule; ledger stays 3)
the wall report XXX.md — a SOFT reading the reviewer may refute or carve (the strongest claim any driver actor may make)

whole-file Why3 proof (SKILL §10.10) + per-method --fun discharge; proof_axiom_allowlist unchanged

disjointness_C1: the fable reviewer holds U+L but NEVER the sub-loop's rationale (its whole value is the independent evidence base); the report author holds only U (it may be tainted — why the reviewer exists); the executor holds the plan + local type-check but never the corpus baseline or the verdict; the driver-verifier holds the acceptance oracles but never the executor's code rationale. No actor can relieve its own constraint.

catchability_C2.caught_by: the fable reviewer (independent U+L, >=1 oracle artifact)
the driver-verifier's three L-planes + the refutation exit

gates.W_wall_escalation: fires the whole workflow, or does NOT. The base-loop sub-agent RETURNS a soft wall-signal {stub, attempts_spent, first_blocker (the exact --fun/type error), cheap_win: bool} — never its in-context rationale (the barrier). Escalate to report->review->impl->execute ONLY if attempts_spent >= the per-stub budget AND cheap_win == false AND the stub is not already CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY in wall-lessons.md AND the cheap queue is empty (Phase 1 drained, base loop reported no_cheap_remaining). Otherwise the base loop handles it inline. This is the cost control AND the barrier.
gates.R_reviewer_independence_with_artifact_te: XXX-response.md is accepted only if BOTH: (a) authored by an actor whose context contained XXX.md + L and provably NOT the sub-loop's rationale (fable spawned with only the report + repo/oracle access); AND (b) it contains >=1 independent ORACLE ARTIFACT (a hand .mlw proven with why3 prove, a byte-diff-sweep, an emit-and-grep of the generated WhyML, or a pycsl --fun run) that CONFIRMS or REFUTES a NAMED factual claim of XXX.md. A prose-only response with zero oracle runs is REJECTED as a rubber stamp. The load-bearing fix: the reviewer's value is a DIFFERENT evidence base (L), not a second opinion on the prose.
gates.P_impl_plan_acceptance: XXX-impl.md is accepted for execution ONLY if its FIRST action is a named make-or-break falsifier spike (the cheapest test that could REFUTE the whole build before any emitter edit) AND it carries an explicit refutation exit ('spike REFUTES -> CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY, stop') AND the three-L-plane gate battery AND honest costed scope. A plan that begins with 'build' or has no refutation branch is REJECTED and re-planned — this prevents 'execute until done' from grinding an impossible wall.
gates.S_impl_plan_spike: XXX-impl.md's FIRST executed action is its make-or-break spike. Verdict routing: PASSES -> proceed to the build; REFUTES -> CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY (record + stop, do NOT build); REFINES (a different blocker) -> re-plan the residual, do not sprawl. 'Cleared' is never asserted without the spike's run.
gates.B_machine_per_increment: all three L-planes pass FRESH (driver-verifier, not the executor's self-report): fidelity AND whole-file Why3 AND byte-diff-0 (or sanctioned-reset + re-proof) AND ledger==3 AND \trusted strictly down AND nothing smuggled (no axiom, no gate loosening, no un-trusted-unverified method).
gates.C_coverage_no_blend: the three planes never blend (a --fun pass never stands in for the whole-file proof; neither stands in for byte-diff-0 or fidelity); non-vacuity (the converted body reads real accessors, no opaque _get_N <hash>); a feature-editing-a-verified-emitter-method carries the §10.4 re-port + re-proof in the SAME increment; every touched stub ends VERIFIED or FLOOR+reason.
gates.S_lesson_skill_consistency_with_concrete: the lesson STORE is a named ledger getting-better/wall-lessons.md (one entry per resolved wall), and for a base-loop-policy-general lesson a CARVE-OUT appended to self-tcb-reduction.md §10 — NEVER an inline edit to the base loop's reasoning. WRITE PROTOCOL: a candidate lesson is checked BEFORE it is written — ignore-signal lessons ('treat X as a wall/noise') get the trigger test (perturb X, does L's verdict move?) -> PASS / CARVE-OUT / REJECT; defer-to-oracle lessons ('on case S do the L-sanctioned action') get the validity test (does L actually distinguish S?). Only PASS or CARVE-OUT is written, WITH the wall it came from, the L-input that revealed the divergence, and (for a carve-out) the exact narrower rule. An over-general lesson is carved to its valid complement, never kept whole; an irreconcilable one is REJECTED and logged (loud-fail).

loop_steps: driver-coordinator runs self-tcb-reduction as a SUB-AGENT in Phase 1 (drain): convert routine cheap stubs until NONE remains, returning either a converted-cheap result (-> commit, stay in Phase 1) or no_cheap_remaining + the residual wall list (stub + measured first blocker), NOT its full rationale. Only no_cheap_remaining advances to step 2.
Gate W -> escalate or continue. On escalate, name the wall XXX (a short slug).
report-author writes the self-contained SOTA report XXX.md (global picture, wall as first seen, deeper truth, SOTA lens, costed routes, honest limits — every claim reproducible from cited evidence).

fable-reviewer (Gate R): spawn a fable sub-agent whose context is XXX.md + repo access to base loop U/L (Why3, byte-diff, pycsl --fun, write+prove a .mlw spike) and NOT the sub-loop's contents. It MUST RUN the oracle and cite >=1 artifact confirming/refuting a named claim. Gate R rejects a prose-only response and re-spawns.

impl-planner synthesizes XXX-impl.md from XXX-response.md + XXX.md. Gate P: accept for execution ONLY if first action is a make-or-break spike with a refutation exit + the three-L-plane battery + costed scope; else re-plan.
executor(s) execute XXX-impl.md (favor rigor). Each leaves edits for the driver-verifier — no commit.

Gate S (spike) -> PASS (build) / REFUTE (CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY, record + stop) / REFINE (re-plan residual). Then per built increment: Gate B (three L-planes FRESH) -> Gate C (no-blend + non-vacuity + §10.4). Verify EVERY agent claim independently.

Verdict: BROKEN (commit the conversions, \trusted down) or CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY (commit report+response+impl+spike evidence, \trusted unchanged, wall recorded). Gate S-lesson on any consolidated lesson. Return to Phase 1; next wall. Never a partial/un-verified commit; never 'grind until done'.

escalation.on_refute_or_sprawl: revert the build to clean + record a gap/lesson; never leave an un-verified tree
escalation.time_aware: in autonomous mode, do not START a full cycle whose fable-review + spike cannot plausibly finish before the deadline — defer it (record the wall-signal for the next run) and spend the tail on cheaper items

stabilizers: rubber-stamped-wrong-report -> Gate R (reviewer gets L not prose; fable barrier) + the impl-plan spike (an independent L-run a prose-only review can't fake)
grind-until-done-on-an-impossible-wall -> the refutation exit: 'done' = BROKEN OR CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY; the impl plan is spike-first; a REFUTE verdict stops the build
agent-over-claim-accepted -> the three-L-plane driver-verifier; the executor never owns a gate verdict; count via grep -F (the ugrep \t trap)
over-general-wall-lesson -> Gate S-lesson (trigger/validity test -> carve-out, never keep-whole)
escalating-a-non-wall (cost blowout) -> Gate W (only genuine, measured, non-cheap walls escalate; cheap queue drained first)
barrier-leak (driver sees sub-loop rationale) -> run self-tcb-reduction as a SUB-AGENT; run the reviewer as a fable sub-agent with only XXX.md+L; both barriers are physical (context), not honorary
feature-edits-a-verified-emitter-method -> Gate C's §10.4 re-port + re-proof in the same increment
sanctioned-but-unproven-shared-theory-change -> the M1 discipline (diff = exactly-the-change AND all affected programs re-prove AND ledger 3), never 'byte-diff nonzero, probably fine'
done_criteria: a wall is RESOLVED when the driver-verifier's gates return BROKEN (all three L-planes green on the conversion, ledger 3, count down) OR CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY (the impl plan's spike REFUTED the build with a reproducible reason). The campaign is at floor when every remaining stub is BROKEN, CERTIFIED-BOUNDARY, or below Gate W (a cheap win the base loop handles). No actor's self-report counts.

oracle_setup.verdict_conjunction: the three L planes + ledger==3 + strictly-decreasing \trusted
per_increment_driver_verifier_fresh: PYTHONHASHSEED=0 python3 src/pycsl/pycsl.py <file> --import-path src/pycsl        # whole-file proof
git worktree add --detach <wt> HEAD; ( cd <wt> && bin/byte-diff-sweep.sh /tmp/before ); bin/byte-diff-sweep.sh /tmp/after && diff -rq /tmp/before /tmp/after   # inertness (or sanctioned reset)
find src/self-annotate/src -name '*.py' -exec grep -cF '\trusted' {} \; | paste -sd+ | bc   # count
oracle_setup.spike_oracle: a hand-written .mlw proven with why3 prove -P alt-ergo (fall back -P z3), asserting the impl plan's make-or-break target is reachable/provable/ledger-clean — run, not argued. Templates: getting-better/composition-wall/*.mlw.
